Definition beck_monadicity : EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A) := {| quasi_inverse := Beck_Inverse ; equivalence_counit := beck_equivalence_counit ; equivalence_unit := beck_equivalence_unit |}.

Class CreatesUSplitCoequalizers {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) := { create_coeq {x y : C} (f g : x ~> y) (S : SplitCoequalizer (fmap[U] f) (fmap[U] g)) : ∃ (q : C) (e : y ~> q), IsCoequalizer f g q e ∧ (∃ i : @Isomorphism D (U q) (scoeq_obj S), to i ∘ fmap[U] e ≈ scoeq_e S); create_coeq_reflects {x y : C} (f g : x ~> y) (S : SplitCoequalizer (fmap[U] f) (fmap[U] g)) (q : C) (e : y ~> q) (He : e ∘ f ≈ e ∘ g) (i : @Isomorphism D (U q) (scoeq_obj S)) (Hi : to i ∘ fmap[U] e ≈ scoeq_e S) : IsCoequalizer f g q e }.

statement_record.book: Theorem 5.5.1 (Beck). A right adjoint U : D -> C is monadic if and only if U creates coequalizers of U-split pairs; equivalently, the comparison K : D -> C^T is an equivalence (resp. isomorphism) iff U creates (resp. strictly creates) coequalizers of U-split pairs.
statement_record.intree: beck_monadicity : EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A), for any adjunction A : F ⊣ U together with CR : CreatesUSplitCoequalizers U; and monadic_creates : CreatesUSplitCoequalizers (EM_Forget T) for the Eilenberg-Moore forgetful functor of any monad T.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the hard half (creates ⇒ K is an equivalence) is complete and even STRONGER in hypothesis economy than many textbook renderings — conservativity is derived from creation (creates_split_reflects_isos, Beck.v:264) rather than assumed — and the in-tree CreatesUSplitCoequalizers is a faithful, non-evil rendering of Riehl's own Definition 5.4.8(b) (existence up to a packaged comparison iso + a reflection clause). What is missing is the converse leg at a GENERAL U: monadic_creates proves it only at U^T = EM_Forget (Riehl's Prop. 5.4.9 in its non-strict form), and the transport along the comparison equivalence that would yield Riehl's Corollary 5.4.10(i) — hence the biconditional — is explicitly deferred in the Beck.v header (lines 106-111). The parenthetical strict variant (K an isomorphism ⟺ U strictly creates) has no in-tree counterpart at all.

gap: The biconditional is not closed at an arbitrary right adjoint. Present: (creates ⇒ monadic) for any adjunction F ⊣ U [beck_monadicity], and (monadic ⇒ creates) only at the canonical U^T = EM_Forget [monadic_creates]. Missing: the transport of monadic_creates along the equivalence K, i.e. 'if U is monadic then U creates coequalizers of U-split pairs' for a general U (Beck.v:106-111 states this is deliberately left to a later development); and the strict form, since the library has no notion of STRICT creation (no on-the-nose unique lift) and no 'K is an isomorphism of categories' statement.

statement_record.book: Definition 5.5.5. A category A is a category of models for an algebraic theory when there is a finitary monadic functor U : A -> Set (monadic with induced monad preserving filtered colimits); such a category is moreover locally finitely presentable, and cHaus is monadic over Set but not of this form.
statement_record.intree: The category of models of a Lawvere theory, Models T C := Sub (Fun (law_cat T) C) Models_sub (finite-product- and terminal-preserving functors out of the theory), with underlying-set functor ev1 : Models T Sets ⟶ Sets; Lawvere_crude_monadicity : EquivalenceOfCategories Lawvere_EM_Comparison, given a left adjoint L ⊣ ev1 T and the three crude-monadicity hypotheses as data.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the library realizes the algebraic-theory side of the concept (models of a Lawvere theory, with the underlying-set functor and a conditional monadicity result), but not the book's DEFINING criterion, which quantifies over finitary monadic functors into Set. 'Finitary' is undefined in tree (no filtered colimits — see riehl:5.5:def4), the monadicity of ev1 is not proved but assumed piecewise (the free-model left adjoint enters as data, plus HasReflexiveCoequalizers/PreservesReflexiveCoequalizers/ReflectsIsos), and the theory ⟷ finitary-monad equivalence that would license the two presentations as interchangeable is explicitly deferred (Theory/Lawvere/Monad.v:59-62, ledger 2).

Definition crude_monadicity : EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A) := {| quasi_inverse := Crude_Inverse ; equivalence_counit := crude_equivalence_counit ; equivalence_unit := crude_equivalence_unit |}.

Definition PreservesReflexiveCoequalizers {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) : Type := ∀ (x y : C) (f g : x ~{C}~> y), ReflexivePair f g → ∀ (q : C) (e : y ~{C}~> q), IsCoequalizer f g q e → IsCoequalizer (fmap[U] f) (fmap[U] g) (U q) (fmap[U] e).
Class HasReflexiveCoequalizers (C : Category) := { reflexive_coeq {x y : C} (f g : x ~> y) : ReflexivePair f g → ∃ (q : C) (e : y ~> q), IsCoequalizer f g q e }.

statement_record.book: Proposition 5.5.8 (reflexive tripleability). Let U : D -> C have a left adjoint. If (i) D has coequalizers of reflexive pairs, (ii) U preserves coequalizers of reflexive pairs, and (iii) U reflects isomorphisms, then U is monadic.
statement_record.intree: Given A : F ⊣ U (F : D ⟶ C, U : C ⟶ D — the library's C is the book's D), RC : HasReflexiveCoequalizers C, pres : PreservesReflexiveCoequalizers U and refl : ReflectsIsos U, crude_monadicity : EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Hypothesis for hypothesis: (i) = HasReflexiveCoequalizers on the domain of U, (ii) = PreservesReflexiveCoequalizers U, (iii) = ReflectsIsos U; the conclusion 'U is monadic' is exactly the payload of Monadic U (Monad/Comparison.v:273 — ∃ F A, EquivalenceOfCategories (EM_Comparison A)), here delivered at the given adjunction, so it is if anything marginally stronger (the equivalence is exhibited at the supplied A rather than merely existentially). Riehl states hypothesis (ii) as preservation of the coequalizers of reflexive pairs and the library states it elementarily (every IsCoequalizer of a reflexive pair is carried to an IsCoequalizer at the image apex); the header (Crude.v:40-50) discloses this as the standard crude hypothesis and explains that the colimit-vocabulary bridge is not needed. Note that the book DEFERS this proof to Exercise 5.5.iii; the library proves it in full.

statement_record.book: Footnote to Proposition 5.5.8: a parallel pair f, g : A -> B is reflexive when both maps admit a common section, i.e. there is s : B -> A with f s = id_B = g s.
